skill.name: connecting-to-logseq
skill.description: Helps configure and troubleshoot Logseq connections through the local HTTP API, Logseq CLI, or an MCP server. It covers token setup, graph paths, backend selection, and connection tests.
skill.summary: Configure and troubleshoot local Logseq connections for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: Static findings are mostly documentation false positives for localhost Logseq examples, Markdown backticks, and graph file names. No prompt injection or external data exfiltration intent was found. Two medium semantic risks remain: token disclosure through echo and unsafe defaults for graph write operations.

remediation.issue: Token checks can print LOGSEQ_API_TOKEN to the terminal.
remediation.suggestion: Replace token echo guidance with redacted presence checks and warn users not to paste token values into logs or support messages.

remediation.issue: Write confirmation and backup defaults are disabled in the sample configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Set confirmWrites and backupBeforeWrite to true by default, and require explicit user confirmation before insert or update actions.

remediation.issue: Setup documentation includes install and build commands for external tooling.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for confirmation before running npm, npx, build, or shell commands, and direct users to verify package sources first.

semantic_findings.title: Token Disclosure Via Echo Command
semantic_findings.description: The troubleshooting flow tells users to run echo $LOGSEQ_API_TOKEN, which prints a secret token to the terminal. This can expose the token in logs, screen shares, or copied support output.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The referenced lines explicitly advise checking the token with echo. The risk is limited to local disclosure, but the value is an authorization secret.

semantic_findings.title: Write Operations Lack Safe Defaults
semantic_findings.description: The documented configuration disables write confirmation and backups while the skill lists Logseq write methods. Users following the defaults could modify graph data without a prompt or backup.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The configuration values are explicit and the same file documents insertBlock as a common method. This is a data-integrity risk rather than evidence of malicious behavior.

content.value_statement: Logseq connection setup often requires tokens, local API settings, and graph paths. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through setup and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to enable Logseq Developer mode and the local HTTP API server.
Shows where to place the Logseq API token and connection settings.
Provides Python, JavaScript, and curl examples for local API calls.
Documents Logseq CLI commands for querying, listing, validating, and exporting graphs.
Lists troubleshooting steps for auth errors, port issues, graph paths, and MCP startup.
limitations: Requires a running Logseq app for HTTP API and MCP workflows.
Does not include the referenced setup scripts or MCP server files in this package.
Requires the user to supply valid API tokens and graph paths.
Write operations can affect local graph data and should be confirmed first.

use_cases.title: Personal Knowledge Setup
use_cases.description: Connect a local Logseq graph to an AI assistant for page lookup, note creation, and task inspection.

use_cases.title: Automation Workflow Planning
use_cases.description: Choose HTTP API, CLI, or MCP access before building local knowledge graph automations.

use_cases.title: Support And Troubleshooting
use_cases.description: Diagnose connection refused, invalid token, graph path, and MCP startup problems with documented checks.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up The HTTP API
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a local Logseq connection.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me connect to Logseq using the local HTTP API. Walk me through enabling the server, creating a token, and testing access.

prompt_templates.title: Fix An Auth Error
prompt_templates.scenario: Troubleshoot a failed API request safely.
prompt_templates.prompt: I get a 401 response from Logseq. Help me verify the token safely without printing the token value.

prompt_templates.title: Choose A Backend
prompt_templates.scenario: Select the best connection method for a workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare HTTP API, CLI, and MCP access for my Logseq workflow. Recommend a backend based on my requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Design A Safe Write Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Logseq automation workflow that can read pages and create blocks. Include confirmation, backup, and rollback steps.

output_examples.input: Help me connect Claude to Logseq.
output: Recommended backend: HTTP API for real-time local access.
Next steps: enable Developer mode, enable the HTTP API server, create a token, and test the current graph call.
Safety note: store the token in an environment variable and avoid printing it.

output_examples.output: The token is missing, revoked, or copied with extra characters. Regenerate it in Logseq, update the environment variable, and test with a redacted token check.

output_examples.input: Should I use CLI or MCP?
output_examples.output: Use CLI for offline graph queries and exports. Use MCP when Claude needs tool-based access through a running Logseq instance.

best_practices: Keep Logseq API tokens in environment variables or secret managers.
Confirm write operations before changing pages or blocks.
Use localhost-only API access and avoid exposing the Logseq port.
anti_patterns: Do not print full API tokens in terminal output or shared logs.
Do not expose the Logseq HTTP API to a public network.
Do not run install or build commands without checking the package source.

faq.question: Does this skill connect to a cloud service?
faq.answer: No. The documented HTTP API endpoint uses Logseq on localhost by default.

faq.question: Can it write to my Logseq graph?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented API methods include block insertion and updates, so confirm writes before use.

faq.question: Do I need an API token?
faq.answer: Yes. The HTTP API and in-app CLI modes require a Logseq authorization token.

faq.question: Does this package include the MCP server?
faq.answer: The reviewed package references an MCP server path, but the scanned files do not include server source files.

faq.question: Can I use the CLI without Logseq running?
faq.answer: Yes. CLI graph operations can work directly against a local graph path.

faq.question: Is it safe to publish my token in config files?
faq.answer: No. Use environment variable references and keep real tokens out of version control.
